page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9i.24xlarge is a general-purpose, enterprise-grade virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture and utilizes dedicated Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors operating at a nominal clock frequency of 3.2 GHz. The instance delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs matched with 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. This balance suits broad compute and memory allocations without favoring one dimension over the other.

Hardware specifications highlight a strictly compute-and-memory configuration without bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, as it includes 0 GPUs and no local disks. All non-volatile persistent storage requirements must be met via external cloud block storage attachments. Networking performance provides a baseline bandwidth capacity of 32 Gbps, offering sufficient throughput for heavy inter-node communication and data ingestion, though no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

The deployment of 96 dedicated Intel cores and 384.0 GB of memory makes the ecs.g9i.24xlarge suited for demanding enterprise services, distributed backend architectures, medium-to-large relational database hosting, large container clusters, and continuous integration workflows. Because it relies entirely on remote storage, architectures must account for network storage latency when designing disk-intensive processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9i.24xlarge is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine built on KVM virtualization and x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors, the instance provides 384.0 GB of memory at an even 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It contains no onboard GPUs and provides no local physical storage, requiring all persistent disks to be provisioned via networked block storage solutions. Network connectivity features a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth, ensuring high throughput for inter-service communication, distributed data operations, and microservice backbones. The instance is suitable for running enterprise application servers, memory-backed multi-tier web applications, continuous integration build clusters, and transactional database workloads that require robust compute parallelism alongside dependable memory capacity without requiring specialized hardware acceleration.
